assumptions: The exact numeric formula for computing infusion rate from blood pressure is not specified; the DSL uses a simple monotonic abstraction: pressure above target lowers flow by one unit and pressure below target raises flow by one unit.
The actual new setpoint value supplied by the caregiver is external to this model; ChangeSetpoint is represented by setting a setpoint_changed flag rather than inventing a target value.

The transition from AutocontrolInit to AutocontrolNormal is modeled as an unguarded completion because the input text names both AutocontrolInit and normal autocontrol but does not specify an initialization-complete event.

Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, Pump Monitors, and shared buffer are modeled through variables and actions within a single mode-control state machine, not as separate concurrent component regions.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch.
The Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy includes an Ask_StartAC submode.
Within Ask_StartAC, pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals.
CA_backManual or any of CB_backManual, CP_backManual, or CC_backManual causes CA_mode to become Manual.
The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver modify target blood pressure.
Patient blood pressure is used to compute the infusion rate.

evidence.summary: All eight hard SL-9 requests were accepted and address the same concrete defect: scenario-injected CARA-scope events InitiateAC, StartAC, ChangeSetpoint, and FaultRemoved could not resolve because the original DSL used local '::' event syntax on those transitions. The candidate changes only those four transitions to ':' event syntax, making Manual -> Ask_StartAC : InitiateAC, Ask_StartAC -> AutocontrolInit : StartAC, Ask_StartAC -> Ask_StartAC : ChangeSetpoint, and PumpFault -> Manual : FaultRemoved visible at CARA scope while preserving their targets and effects.

The repaired DSL satisfies the failing scenario obligations described in the FixLog: InitiateAC from Manual can enter Ask_StartAC with CA_mode=1 and control_released=0; StartAC from Ask_StartAC can enter AutocontrolInit with CA_mode=2 and setpoint_changed reset by AutocontrolInit.enter; ChangeSetpoint can remain in Ask_StartAC and set setpoint_changed=1; FaultRemoved from PumpFault can recover to Manual while clearing pump_fault and alarm_signal, after which Manual actions restore shared_sensor_buffer, pump_speed, and flow_rate.

The diff is minimal and does not drop NL-required model content. Required states Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault remain. Required variables including CA_mode, target_bp, blood_pressure, shared_sensor_buffer, built_in_switch, control_voltage, pump_speed, flow_rate, pump_fault, alarm_signal, control_released, and log_count remain. Manual pump control, autocontrol pressure-to-flow behavior, logging, fault alarm/release behavior, TerminateAC transitions, and cross-component backManual fallbacks are preserved.

No scenario regression is reported by local_check_evidence. The local rejection is not a behavioral regression but a missing_required_grounding matcher finding for transition:InitialToManual and transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault, both of which are visibly present and unchanged in the candidate DSL.

The local rejection reason is therefore a conservative grounding/design matcher issue, not evidence that the repaired behavior drops a required NL obligation. evidence: NL requires caregiver modification of target blood pressure and setpoint change in Ask_StartAC.
DSL has no assignment to `target_bp` after initialization.
ChangeSetpoint effect is only `setpoint_changed = 1`.
Simulation oracle validates target remaining `80` after ChangeSetpoint.
blocking_findings.summary: The required caregiver setpoint/target blood-pressure modification is not implemented; ChangeSetpoint only sets a flag while the control target remains constant.

evidence: Global `! * -> Manual` fallback transitions apply from PumpFault.
Manual.enter clears `alarm_signal`; Manual.during restores `pump_speed` and `flow_rate`.
Only `FaultRemoved` clears `pump_fault`, but forced fallback does not.
Passed scenarios show Manual with `pump_fault: 1` and `alarm_signal: 0` after fallback from PumpFault.
blocking_findings.summary: Forced fallback can recover from PumpFault to Manual, clear the alarm, and restore manual pump outputs while the fault remains active.

evidence: NL: "The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver modify target blood pressure" and "within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed".
DSL: `def int target_bp = 80;` with no assignment to `target_bp` anywhere after initialization.
DSL: `Ask_StartAC -> Ask_StartAC : ChangeSetpoint effect { setpoint_changed = 1; };`
Simulation oracle confirms unchanged target: `change_setpoint_stays_in_ask_and_flags_change` has `target_bp: 80` after ChangeSetpoint.
findings.summary: The caregiver target blood-pressure modification is not faithfully modeled: ChangeSetpoint only sets a flag while target_bp remains constant, even though target_bp is used by the infusion-rate calculation.

evidence: NL: "If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault".
DSL: global forced transitions `! * -> Manual :: CA_backManual;`, `CB_backManual`, `CP_backManual`, `CC_backManual` apply from PumpFault as well.
DSL Manual.enter sets `alarm_signal = 0`; Manual.during sets `pump_speed = built_in_switch` and `flow_rate = default_flow_rate` without guarding on `pump_fault`.
Simulation `cc_back_manual_fallback_from_pumpfault` passes with `actual_state: CARA.Manual`, `pump_fault: 1`, `alarm_signal: 0`, `pump_speed: 17`, `flow_rate: 6`.
Simulation `ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe` similarly passes with `pump_fault: 1` and `alarm_signal: 0`.
findings.summary: Forced fallback from PumpFault to Manual can clear the alarm and resume manual outputs while pump_fault remains asserted, creating an unsafe recovery path inconsistent with fault-removal-before-recovery behavior.

evidence: NL names coordinated runtime components: Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, Pump Monitors, and infusion pump.
DSL contains one composite state `CARA` with five leaf states and variables, not separate component regions.

`five_component_summary` is empty.
findings.summary: The model covers several behavioral aspects of the Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, and Pump/Pump Monitors through variables and actions, but it does not decompose or coordinate the named runtime components as distinct concurrent component regions.

evidence: DSL declares external-like quantities as ordinary variables: `blood_pressure`, `built_in_switch`, `control_voltage`, `pump_fault`, `default_flow_rate`.

NL distinguishes external/caregiver inputs and sensor readings from outputs such as pump speed, flow rate, alarms, logs, and control release.
findings.summary: External inputs and component roles are not clearly separated from internal variables and outputs, reducing traceability for caregiver actions, sensor readings, pump fault inputs, and actuator outputs.

findings.summary: The infusion-rate algorithm and logging are very coarse abstractions; this is acceptable as an abstraction only if explicitly capped, but it should not be treated as a strong behavioral reference.

evidence.summary: Both current hard SL-7 model-review requests were accepted by SL-9 and are directly addressed in the candidate DSL. For the NL-fidelity request, the candidate adds `caregiver_target_bp` as the caregiver-supplied setpoint input and changes `Ask_StartAC -> Ask_StartAC : ChangeSetpoint` to assign `target_bp = caregiver_target_bp` while preserving `setpoint_changed = 1`, the self-transition, and the prior CARA-scope event repair. This resolves the reviewed defect that ChangeSetpoint previously only set a flag and never modified the NL-required target blood pressure.

For the unsafe-recovery request, the candidate preserves all required backManual fallback transitions and Manual as the shared recovery target, but makes Manual fault-aware. `Manual.enter` and `Manual.during` now keep `alarm_signal = 1` and suppress `pump_speed` and `flow_rate` while `pump_fault` remains active; once `FaultRemoved` clears `pump_fault`, Manual operation resumes built-in-switch pump speed and default flow rate. This matches the NL sequence that pump faults activate alarms, the caregiver removes the fault, and then software/manual recovery proceeds.

The diff is small and preserves required NL-grounded content: states Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault remain; required variables including CA_mode, target_bp, blood_pressure, shared_sensor_buffer, built_in_switch, control_voltage, pump_speed, flow_rate, pump_fault, alarm_signal, control_released, and log_count remain; initial Manual entry, InitiateAC, StartAC, ChangeSetpoint, AutocontrolInit completion, guarded AutocontrolNormal-to-PumpFault, FaultRemoved, TerminateAC, and all four backManual fallbacks remain represented.

The prior FixLog repair_memory recorded an SL-10 override of a conservative local missing_required_grounding objection for `transition:InitialToManual` and `transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault`. The current candidate preserves the same concrete lines, `[*] -> Manual;` and `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];`, so that remembered objection remains audit-only and is not reopened by a DSL deletion or weakening.

Local deterministic simulation now reports 13/15 scenarios passing and flags failures only in scenarios that expect the previously unsafe behavior: `cc_back_manual_fallback_from_pumpfault` and `ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe` expected Manual with `pump_fault` still asserted but `alarm_signal = 0`, pump outputs restored; the candidate instead produces Manual with `alarm_signal = 1`, `pump_speed = 0`, and `flow_rate = 0`. That local expected-vs-actual difference is the intended repair for the hard SL-7 unsafe-recovery finding, not an NL-fidelity regression.

decisions.rationale: Rejected as unsafe/inconsistent with the current NL-grounded model and prior accepted verification evidence. In scenario terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual, failing step completion_to_normal_for_terminate expects CARA.AutocontrolNormal with flow_rate=11 when blood_pressure=78, target_bp=80, and default_flow_rate=9, while the current monotonic abstraction computes default_flow_rate + 1 = 10 for low pressure. evidence.summary: The candidate directly implements the locked SL-10 rework guidance from fixlog-8: it removes the duplicate global forced `! * -> Manual : CA_backManual` coverage and replaces it with deterministic explicit `CA_backManual` transitions from Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault. The PumpFault-specific CA_backManual transition clears `pump_fault` and `alarm_signal`, resolving the prior CA_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe ambiguity without retaining the W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL duplicate.

The candidate keeps the accepted Manual self-transition on `FaultRemoved` with effect `{ pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }`, so after `CC_backManual` reaches Manual with an uncleared fault, a later `FaultRemoved` can clear the fault and allow Manual actions to restore `shared_sensor_buffer`, `pump_speed = built_in_switch`, and `flow_rate = default_flow_rate`. This matches the NL sequence that pump faults alarm, the caregiver removes the fault, and manual recovery proceeds.

The candidate preserves the NL-required model structure and behavior: states Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault remain; required variables remain; `[ * ] -> Manual` remains as the initial manual default; `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0]` remains for pump complications; InitiateAC, StartAC, ChangeSetpoint assigning `target_bp = caregiver_target_bp`, TerminateAC transitions, FaultRemoved recovery, manual pump-output actions, autocontrol control-voltage pump speed, logging, and pressure-to-flow monotonic behavior are preserved.

Local simulation improves from the prior 13/15 to 14/15 scenarios passing. The only remaining scenario mismatch is `terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual`, step `completion_to_normal_for_terminate`, where local expected `flow_rate=11` but actual is `flow_rate=10` for `blood_pressure=78`, `target_bp=80`, and `default_flow_rate=9`. The FixLog repeatedly records that the accepted NL-grounded abstraction is a one-unit monotonic adjustment, so low pressure yields `default_flow_rate + 1 = 10`; changing it to 11 would be an ungrounded +2 adjustment and could regress other accepted low-pressure autocontrol behavior.

The complete FixLog and repair_memory show that previous objections about `transition:InitialToManual` and `transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault` were already audited as conservative grounding matcher findings because the concrete DSL lines are visibly present. The current candidate still preserves those lines. The new `transition:CA_backManualFallback` matcher objection is similarly a representation/count issue rather than a loss of NL behavior: CA_backManual remains concretely represented for every current CARA state, and `CA_mode` becomes Manual through Manual entry on each fallback target.

local_override_rationale: Local_check_evidence reports `scenario_regression; forced_transition_count_drift; missing_required_grounding`, with `target_resolved=false`, `regression_detected=true`, and `drift_risk='major'`. The scenario_regression portion is not a true NL-fidelity regression: the only failing scenario is `terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual`, step `completion_to_normal_for_terminate`, where local expected `flow_rate=11` but actual `flow_rate=10`. The NL says higher pressure lowers flow and lower pressure raises flow, without specifying a numeric +2 rule. The accepted FixLog abstraction is a one-unit monotonic adjustment, so `default_flow_rate=9` and below-target pressure correctly produce `flow_rate=10`. SL-9 explicitly preserved this formula to avoid an ungrounded benchmark-specific edit.

The `forced_transition_count_drift` objection is an expected and intended result of the locked rework from fixlog-8, not evidence of lost behavior. The prior candidate was rejected because global forced `CA_backManual` and a source-specific `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual` duplicated the same event/source/target and triggered W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL. The current candidate removes the problematic global CA forced line and replaces it with explicit deterministic CA_backManual transitions for Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault. This reduces the forced-transition count but preserves the NL-required CA_backManual recovery behavior while eliminating the design ambiguity.

The `missing_required_grounding` objection for `transition:InitialToManual` and `transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault` repeats the previously overridden conservative matcher issue. The candidate DSL visibly contains `[ * ] -> Manual;` and `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];`; neither was deleted or weakened. These concrete lines satisfy the NL requirements for default manual mode and pump-fault transition during normal autocontrol.

The `missing_required_grounding` objection for `transition:CA_backManualFallback` is also a matcher/count abstraction issue rather than a behavior loss. Although the single global forced `! * -> Manual : CA_backManual` line was intentionally removed to resolve W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL, CA_backManual is now represented by explicit transitions from every concrete CARA state in this hierarchy: `Manual -> Manual`, `Ask_StartAC -> Manual`, `AutocontrolInit -> Manual`, `AutocontrolNormal -> Manual`, and `PumpFault -> Manual`. Each target is Manual, and Manual entry sets `CA_mode = 0`, satisfying the NL cross-component fallback requirement that CA_backManual causes CA_mode to become Manual.

The current candidate resolves the remembered fixlog-8 objections: it eliminates the forced/normal duplicate, preserves safe CC_backManual behavior with the fault still active until FaultRemoved, keeps the Manual FaultRemoved self-transition, preserves the accepted low-pressure formula, and preserves required grounded states/transitions/actions. Therefore the local major rejection is explainable as an invalid local flow expectation plus conservative grounding/count matchers, and the repaired DSL is acceptable for the next full top-down revalidation pass.

local_override_rationale: Local_check_evidence reports `scenario_regression; forced_transition_count_drift; missing_required_grounding`, with `target_resolved=false`, `regression_detected=true`, and `drift_risk='major'`. The scenario_regression portion is not a true NL-fidelity regression: the only failing scenario is `terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual`, step `completion_to_normal_for_terminate`, where local expected `flow_rate=11` but actual `flow_rate=10`. The NL says higher pressure lowers flow and lower pressure raises flow, without specifying a numeric +2 rule. The accepted FixLog abstraction is a one-unit monotonic adjustment, so `default_flow_rate=9` and below-target pressure correctly produce `flow_rate=10`. SL-9 explicitly preserved this formula to avoid an ungrounded benchmark-specific edit.

The `forced_transition_count_drift` objection is an expected and intended result of the locked rework from fixlog-8, not evidence of lost behavior. The prior candidate was rejected because global forced `CA_backManual` and a source-specific `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual` duplicated the same event/source/target and triggered W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL. The current candidate removes the problematic global CA forced line and replaces it with explicit deterministic CA_backManual transitions for Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault. This reduces the forced-transition count but preserves the NL-required CA_backManual recovery behavior while eliminating the design ambiguity.

The `missing_required_grounding` objection for `transition:InitialToManual` and `transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault` repeats the previously overridden conservative matcher issue. The candidate DSL visibly contains `[ * ] -> Manual;` and `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];`; neither was deleted or weakened. These concrete lines satisfy the NL requirements for default manual mode and pump-fault transition during normal autocontrol.

The `missing_required_grounding` objection for `transition:CA_backManualFallback` is also a matcher/count abstraction issue rather than a behavior loss. Although the single global forced `! * -> Manual : CA_backManual` line was intentionally removed to resolve W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL, CA_backManual is now represented by explicit transitions from every concrete CARA state in this hierarchy: `Manual -> Manual`, `Ask_StartAC -> Manual`, `AutocontrolInit -> Manual`, `AutocontrolNormal -> Manual`, and `PumpFault -> Manual`. Each target is Manual, and Manual entry sets `CA_mode = 0`, satisfying the NL cross-component fallback requirement that CA_backManual causes CA_mode to become Manual.

The current candidate resolves the remembered fixlog-8 objections: it eliminates the forced/normal duplicate, preserves safe CC_backManual behavior with the fault still active until FaultRemoved, keeps the Manual FaultRemoved self-transition, preserves the accepted low-pressure formula, and preserves required grounded states/transitions/actions. Therefore the local major rejection is explainable as an invalid local flow expectation plus conservative grounding/count matchers, and the repaired DSL is acceptable for the next full top-down revalidation pass.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Preserve the accepted low-pressure autocontrol formula default_flow_rate + 1; do not introduce an ungrounded +2 adjustment.']
decisions.rationale: Accepted for rework tracking without changing the DSL flow formula. In terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual, step completion_to_normal_for_terminate expected CARA.AutocontrolNormal with flow_rate=11, but the actual flow_rate=10 comes from the preserved NL-grounded monotonic abstraction: blood_pressure below target_bp raises flow_rate by one unit, so default_flow_rate=9 becomes 10. Changing this to 11 would contradict the prior accepted evidence and regress the low-pressure autocontrol scenario. The repair therefore preserves the correct formula and documents that this scenario expectation should be treated as the invalid local expectation.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Add Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }.']
decisions.rationale: Accepted. In cc_back_manual_fallback_from_pumpfault, the first step correctly reaches Manual with pump_fault still active, alarm_signal=1, pump_speed=0, and flow_rate=0. The failing step fault_removed_then_manual_outputs_restore injects CARA.FaultRemoved while already in Manual, but the DSL only handled FaultRemoved from PumpFault. The smallest safe repair is a Manual self-transition on the CARA-scope FaultRemoved event that clears pump_fault and alarm_signal so Manual actions restore shared_sensor_buffer, pump_speed from built_in_switch, and flow_rate from default_flow_rate.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Remove the global forced CA_backManual transition so it no longer duplicates PumpFault -> Manual on the same event.', 'Add explicit CA_backManual fallback transitions for Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault.', 'Give only the PumpFault CA_backManual transition the fault-clearing effect needed for the CA-specific probe.']
decisions.rationale: Accepted. In ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe, CARA.CA_backManual from PumpFault reached Manual but left pump_fault active, so Manual fault-aware actions kept alarm_signal=1, pump_speed=0, and flow_rate=0 instead of the expected cleared-fault manual outputs. The repair removes the duplicate global forced CA_backManual coverage and replaces it with deterministic explicit CA_backManual transitions for Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, and AutocontrolNormal, plus a single PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual transition that clears pump_fault and alarm_signal. This resolves W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL while preserving the CA shared recovery target.

diff_summary.summary: Removed the global forced CA_backManual line and replaced it with explicit deterministic CA_backManual transitions for Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault; the PumpFault CA_backManual transition clears pump_fault and alarm_signal. Added Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved to clear an already-reached Manual fault state. Preserved CB/CP/CC forced fallbacks, safe CC fault behavior, the accepted low-pressure +1 flow formula, initial Manual transition, guarded AutocontrolNormal-to-PumpFault transition, and all required grounded states/variables/actions.

repair_rationale: Addressed fixlog-8 rework by eliminating W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL: the single global forced CA_backManual fallback was removed, so there is no longer duplicate forced and normal coverage for CARA.PumpFault -> CARA.Manual on CARA.CA_backManual.

Preserved deterministic CA_backManual behavior with explicit non-PumpFault transitions: Manual -> Manual, Ask_StartAC -> Manual, AutocontrolInit -> Manual, and AutocontrolNormal -> Manual all keep Manual as the shared recovery target and still re-enter/enter Manual so manual outputs are restored when pump_fault is clear.

For ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe, the failing actual values were alarm_signal=1, pump_speed=0, and flow_rate=0 because pump_fault stayed active. The PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual effect now clears pump_fault and alarm_signal before Manual runs, so Manual restores shared_sensor_buffer, pump_speed=built_in_switch, and flow_rate=default_flow_rate.

For cc_back_manual_fallback_from_pumpfault, CC_backManual remains a forced fallback and intentionally preserves the safe active-fault behavior on the first step. The added Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved transition handles the second step by clearing pump_fault and alarm_signal after the caregiver removes the fault, allowing Manual actions to restore outputs.

For terminate_ac_from_ask_and_init_returns_manual, the flow_rate=11 expectation is not implemented because it conflicts with the accepted NL-grounded monotonic abstraction. With blood_pressure=78, target_bp=80, and default_flow_rate=9, the preserved formula correctly yields flow_rate=10; changing it would regress normal_autocontrol_low_pressure_raises_flow and other accepted evidence.

Required grounding is preserved: transition:InitialToManual remains represented by [*] -> Manual;, and transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault remains represented by ! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];. All required states, variables, TerminateAC transitions, InitiateAC, StartAC, ChangeSetpoint with target_bp=caregiver_target_bp, FaultRemoved recovery, and manual/autocontrol pump-output actions remain present.

evidence: DSL variable `pump_fault` abstracts all pump-operation complications including fluid-tubing occlusion.

evidence.summary: The hard SL-7 request is directly resolved. The request identified `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }` as unsafe because it conflated fallback-to-Manual with the NL-required caregiver fault-removal step. The candidate changes that transition to `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual;`, preserving Manual as the recovery target while leaving `pump_fault` and `alarm_signal` unchanged until `FaultRemoved` occurs.

The candidate preserves the explicit caregiver fault-removal paths required by the NL: `PumpFault -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }` and `Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }`. Manual remains fault-aware, so while `pump_fault > 0` it keeps `alarm_signal = 1` and suppresses `pump_speed` and `flow_rate`; after `FaultRemoved`, Manual restores sensor buffering, built-in-switch pump speed, and default flow rate.

The required grounded structure is preserved in the DSL: states Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault remain; variables including CA_mode, target_bp, blood_pressure, shared_sensor_buffer, built_in_switch, control_voltage, pump_speed, flow_rate, pump_fault, alarm_signal, control_released, and log_count remain; `[ * ] -> Manual`, `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0]`, InitiateAC, StartAC, ChangeSetpoint with `target_bp = caregiver_target_bp`, TerminateAC transitions, and backManual recovery paths remain represented.

The complete FixLog shows earlier SL-10 passes overrode conservative local expectations and then a later hard SL-7 review reopened the CA_backManual-from-PumpFault behavior as unsafe. The current SL-9 decision correctly follows the new hard request rather than the older local probe that expected CA_backManual to clear the fault. This is a legitimate NL-fidelity correction, not an ungrounded regression.

The only substantive DSL behavior change is the removal of the fault-clearing effect from `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual`; the added `pump_speed = 0` in PumpFault.enter is consistent with pump-fault safe output suppression and does not drop any NL-required behavior.

local_override_rationale: Local_check_evidence reports `scenario_regression; missing_required_grounding`, with `target_resolved=false`, `regression_detected=true`, and `drift_risk='major'`. The scenario regression is the local scenario `ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_forced_line_probe`, step `ca_backmanual_from_pumpfault_to_manual`, which expected `alarm_signal=0`, `pump_speed=18`, and `flow_rate=7` immediately after `CARA.CA_backManual` from PumpFault while the initial fault was active. That expected behavior is exactly what the current hard SL-7 review rejected as unsafe: CA_backManual must not silently perform caregiver fault removal.

The NL states that if a pump fault occurs, the pump activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault, and when CARA was controlling the pump the software releases control. It separately states that CA_backManual makes CA_mode become Manual as the shared recovery target. It does not require CA_backManual to clear `pump_fault` or restore pump outputs before `FaultRemoved`. The candidate’s actual local behavior—Manual state with `alarm_signal=1`, `pump_speed=0`, and `flow_rate=0` until FaultRemoved—is therefore more faithful to the NL fault-removal ordering than the local expected values.

The previous repair_memory and FixLog recorded that local probes had once expected CA_backManual from PumpFault to clear the fault, but the current hard model-review request explicitly supersedes that local-only expectation by identifying it as unsafe recovery. Passing this candidate is not ignoring the remembered objection; it resolves the newly reopened hard objection by separating fallback-to-Manual from explicit `FaultRemoved` recovery while preserving Manual as the CA_backManual target.

The local `missing_required_grounding` finding for `transition:InitialToManual` and `transition:AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault` is the same conservative matcher issue previously audited in FixLog. The candidate visibly preserves `[ * ] -> Manual;` and `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];`, so no required transition was deleted or weakened.

The local `missing_required_grounding` finding for `transition:CA_backManualFallback` is also a representation/matcher issue rather than behavior loss. The candidate preserves explicit CA_backManual transitions from Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault, each targeting Manual; Manual.enter sets `CA_mode = 0`. Thus the NL-required CA_backManual shared recovery target remains concretely represented even without a single global forced CA_backManual line.

The candidate does not reintroduce the earlier W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL duplicate: there is no global forced CA_backManual line duplicating the PumpFault-specific CA_backManual transition. It preserves the accepted one-unit pressure-to-flow abstraction and all previously required states, events, variables, guards, and actions. The local major rejection is therefore explained by an unsafe/outdated scenario oracle plus conservative grounding matching, not by a real NL regression.

decisions.accepted_edit_intent: ['Change `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; };` to `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual;`.', 'Preserve `PumpFault -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; };` and `Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; };` as the explicit caregiver fault-removal paths.']
decisions.rationale: Accepted. The hard SL-7 review evidence identifies that `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; }` conflates CA_backManual fallback-to-manual with the NL-required separate caregiver fault removal. The smallest safe edit preserves the CA_backManual recovery target Manual but removes the fault-clearing effect from that transition, so an active pump fault remains alarmed and output-suppressed in Manual until the explicit `FaultRemoved` transition clears it.

diff_summary.summary: Removed the fault-clearing effect from the PumpFault CA_backManual transition, preserving the Manual recovery target while requiring explicit FaultRemoved to clear pump_fault and alarm_signal. All required states, variables, fallback events, FaultRemoved transitions, initial Manual entry, autocontrol fault transition, setpoint update, and pressure-to-flow behavior are preserved.

repair_rationale: Hard request `fixreq-3-sl7-0-65d2e7f559` is resolved by separating CA_backManual fallback from caregiver fault removal: `PumpFault -> Manual : CA_backManual;` now changes the state to Manual without clearing `pump_fault` or `alarm_signal`.

The explicit fault-removal semantics remain grounded and available through `PumpFault -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; };` and `Manual -> Manual : FaultRemoved effect { pump_fault = 0; alarm_signal = 0; };`.

Manual remains fault-aware: if `pump_fault > 0`, Manual keeps `alarm_signal = 1` and suppresses `pump_speed` and `flow_rate`; after `FaultRemoved`, Manual restores `pump_speed = built_in_switch` and `flow_rate = default_flow_rate`.

The latest waived local objections about the stale `flow_rate=11` scenario, forced-transition count drift, and conservative grounding matcher are audit-only per SL-10; this repair does not change the accepted one-unit low-pressure flow formula or reintroduce the rejected global forced CA_backManual duplicate.

Required preserved elements remain represented: `[ * ] -> Manual` is preserved as `[ * ] -> Manual;`, `AutocontrolNormalToPumpFault` is preserved as `! AutocontrolNormal -> PumpFault : if [pump_fault > 0];`, and CA/CB/CP/CC backManual recovery paths still target Manual.

scenario_results.name: normal_autocontrol_low_pressure_raises_flow

scenario_results.name: normal_autocontrol_no_fault_no_phantom_fault_transition

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in Ask_StartAC verifies TerminateAC returns to Manual from Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, and AutocontrolNormal while releasing control.

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in AutocontrolNormal verifies caregiver TerminateAC releases algorithmic pump control and returns to Manual.
scenario_results.name: terminate_ac_from_normal_returns_manual

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in Ask_StartAC sweeps CA_backManual, CB_backManual, and CP_backManual fallbacks from distinct autocontrol-related states to Manual.
scenario_results.name: back_manual_fallbacks_from_autocontrol_states

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in PumpFault verifies CC_backManual shares Manual as recovery target while an uncleared fault keeps alarm active until FaultRemoved.
scenario_results.name: cc_back_manual_fallback_from_pumpfault

scenario_results.name: direct_change_setpoint_self_transition_effect_probe
